# TalkLive

> TalkLive (https://talklive.app) is a browser-based random chat service for adults, offering one-to-one voice calls and text chat. Core matching is free and does not require an account. Voice uses encrypted WebRTC over a TURN relay in production and is not recorded or stored by TalkLive. Typed messages and related context may be retained for a limited rolling period as described in the Privacy Policy.

Key facts: voice-only or text-only modes; optional country and interest preferences do not guarantee a specific match; matching is instant for everyone; optional Premium is announced but not yet available for purchase; no video chat; 18+ policy; leave, block and report controls. Participant identity, age, location and intent are not verified.

## Common uses
- Talking to someone new by voice without a camera, phone number or app install (works in any mobile or desktop browser).
- Practising spoken English (or another language) with real people: see [Practice English Speaking](https://talklive.app/practice-english-speaking) and [Language Exchange](https://talklive.app/language-exchange).
- A free, voice-first [Omegle alternative](https://talklive.app/omegle-alternative) for adults, with text chat for people who prefer typing.
- Late-night conversation when friends are asleep: see [Late Night Chat](https://talklive.app/late-night-chat).
- Keeping in touch with people you click with through the built-in Friends feature, without exchanging phone numbers.

## Who uses TalkLive (as of October 2026)
- Visitors from about 170 countries in a typical month. The largest groups are from India, the United States, Pakistan, China, Egypt, Bangladesh, the United Kingdom, Nigeria, Germany and Saudi Arabia.
- About 70% of visitors are on a phone. Most conversations are in English; Chinese, Arabic, French, Spanish, Russian and German are the next most common interface languages.
- Matching prefers people with shared interests and then people using the same interface language, but never makes anyone wait for a match.
- Text chat is used more than voice; mini games (Tic Tac Toe, Dots & Boxes), reactions, GIFs and a friends list are built in.

## Main pages
- [TalkLive app](https://talklive.app/): Start a random voice or text chat instantly.

## Guides
- [Talk to Strangers](https://talklive.app/talk-to-strangers): Talk to strangers by voice or text, free and without an account. What the first five minutes of a conversation with someone new are really like, minute by minute, and what research says about each one.
- [Random Voice Chat](https://talklive.app/random-voice-chat): Free random voice chat with strangers: one tap to talk with someone new, audio only, no camera or account. Why a voice carries more than text or video, according to the research.
- [Random Text Chat](https://talklive.app/random-text-chat): Free one-to-one text chat with people worldwide: tap to chat and get paired with someone new, no microphone and no sign-up, adults 18+. Why typing to a stranger works, from IRC to now.
- [Anonymous Chat](https://talklive.app/anonymous-chat): Free anonymous chat with strangers by voice or text - no account, phone number or camera. Exactly what the other person sees, what they never see, and what TalkLive keeps, item by item.
- [Random Call](https://talklive.app/random-call): Make a free random call to another adult from your browser: no phone number, no app, no calling credit. How the call is connected, how much data it uses, and how to fix the usual problems.
- [Talk to Someone](https://talklive.app/talk-to-someone): Need someone to talk to right now? Have a free, anonymous conversation by voice or text with another adult, with no sign-up - and where to find trained support if it is urgent.
- [Late Night Chat](https://talklive.app/late-night-chat): Can't sleep? Late night voice and text chat with people around the world, free and without an account. Where it is still evening when it is 2 a.m. for you, and how to look after yourself at night.
- [Make Friends Online](https://talklive.app/make-friends-online): Make friends online through real conversations, not profiles. What research says about how many hours a friendship takes, and how TalkLive helps you keep the people you click with - free, no sign-up to start.
- [Practice English Speaking](https://talklive.app/practice-english-speaking): Practise speaking English for free in real conversations with people around the world. Why speaking (not just listening) builds fluency, a phrase bank for real calls, and how to make five minutes count.
- [Language Exchange](https://talklive.app/language-exchange): Free language exchange by voice or text: trade ten minutes of your language for ten of theirs with someone new. The tandem method's two rules, a ready-made script, and how to correct each other well.
- [Voice Chat vs Video Chat](https://talklive.app/voice-chat-vs-video-chat): Voice chat vs video chat, round by round: privacy, data, fatigue, safety with strangers, emotion and identity. An honest scorecard - including where video wins - and why TalkLive chose voice.
- [Omegle Alternative](https://talklive.app/omegle-alternative): Omegle closed on 8 November 2023. How to judge any Omegle alternative before you trust it - six checks - and how TalkLive, a free voice and text chat for adults with no camera, measures up.
- [How TalkLive Works](https://talklive.app/how-it-works): How TalkLive connects two strangers: the live queues, how matching and preferences work, how WebRTC and the TURN relay carry encrypted audio, how text is delivered, and what "not recorded" does and does not mean.
- [Safety Center](https://talklive.app/safety): How to stay safe on TalkLive: five rules, what to do if a conversation goes wrong, what TalkLive records and does not record, how reporting and blocking work, and where to get help.
- [Languages](https://talklive.app/language-chat-guide): Use TalkLive in 17 languages, including right-to-left Arabic, Persian and Urdu. How the interface language works, how to find people who speak your language, and tips for talking across languages.
- [Countries](https://talklive.app/country-chat-guide): Guides to talking with people in 21 countries - India, the US, Pakistan, China, Egypt, the UK, Nigeria, Germany, Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and more - and how country matching works.
- [All Guides](https://talklive.app/resources): Every TalkLive guide in one place: talking to strangers, voice and text chat, safety and privacy, making friends, languages and country guides - and the editorial standards they are written to.

## Country guides
- [India](https://talklive.app/countries/india): Free voice and text chat with people in India - Hindi, English or Hinglish, no sign-up, no camera. Why India talks to strangers like it talks on a long train, and when India is online (IST).
- [Pakistan](https://talklive.app/countries/pakistan): Free voice and text chat with people in Pakistan - Urdu, Punjabi or English, no sign-up, no camera, with an Urdu interface. Why Pakistan talks late, and when it is online (PKT).
- [Bangladesh](https://talklive.app/countries/bangladesh): Free voice and text chat with people in Bangladesh and Bangla speakers worldwide - no sign-up, no camera, with a Bangla interface. On adda, the language people died for, and when Bangladesh is online.
- [United States](https://talklive.app/countries/united-states): Free voice and text chat with people in the United States - no sign-up, no camera, no phone number. America's long love affair with talking to strangers, and when Americans are online in every time zone.
- [United Kingdom](https://talklive.app/countries/united-kingdom): Free voice and text chat with people in the UK - no sign-up, no camera, no phone number. Why British evenings are TalkLive's busiest hours, the weather-talk ritual, and how to get chatting.
- [Egypt](https://talklive.app/countries/egypt): Free voice and text chat with people in Egypt - Egyptian Arabic or English, no sign-up, no camera, with an Arabic interface. Umm Kulthum, the ahwa, and when Egypt is online in Cairo time.
- [Nigeria](https://talklive.app/countries/nigeria): Free voice and text chat with people in Nigeria - English, Pidgin, Yoruba, Igbo or Hausa, no sign-up, no camera, light on data. Achebe on conversation, and when Nigeria is online (WAT).
- [Indonesia](https://talklive.app/countries/indonesia): Free voice and text chat with people in Indonesia - Bahasa Indonesia or English, no sign-up, no app to install, no camera, with an Indonesian interface. Basa-basi, nongkrong, and when Indonesia is online (WIB).
- [Germany](https://talklive.app/countries/germany): Free voice and text chat with people in Germany - in German or English, no sign-up, no camera, with a German interface. Feierabend, du or Sie, and when Germany is online in German time.
- [Saudi Arabia](https://talklive.app/countries/saudi-arabia): Free voice and text chat with people in Saudi Arabia - in Arabic or English, no sign-up, no camera, with an Arabic interface. The majlis, Saudi coffee, Ramadan nights and when the Kingdom is online.
- [Morocco](https://talklive.app/countries/morocco): Free voice and text chat with people in Morocco - in Darija, French, Arabic or English, no sign-up, no camera. Mint tea, the language that borrows from everyone, and when Morocco is online.
- [United Arab Emirates](https://talklive.app/countries/united-arab-emirates): Free voice and text chat with people in the UAE - in English, Arabic, Hindi, Urdu, Tagalog or Malayalam, no sign-up, no camera. Who lives in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, and when the Emirates are online.
- [Canada](https://talklive.app/countries/canada): Free voice and text chat with people in Canada - in English or French, no sign-up, no camera. Six time zones, two official languages, a country of newcomers, and when Canada is online.
- [Philippines](https://talklive.app/countries/philippines): Free voice and text chat with people in the Philippines - in Filipino, English, Taglish or Bisaya, no sign-up, no camera. Kwentuhan, the night shift, and when the Philippines is online.
- [China](https://talklive.app/countries/china): Free voice and text chat with people in China - in Mandarin or English, no sign-up, no camera. Phrases, topics, safety and when China is online on Beijing time.
- [Turkey](https://talklive.app/countries/turkey): Free voice and text chat with people in Turkey - in Turkish or English, no sign-up, no camera. Tea, football, dizi, two continents and when Turkey is online.
- [Brazil](https://talklive.app/countries/brazil): Free voice and text chat with people in Brazil - bate-papo in Portuguese or English, no sign-up, no camera. Slang, football, music and when Brazil is online.
- [Mexico](https://talklive.app/countries/mexico): Free voice and text chat with people in Mexico - platica in Spanish or English, no sign-up, no camera. Slang, food, football and when Mexico is online.
- [Malaysia](https://talklive.app/countries/malaysia): Free voice and text chat with people in Malaysia - in Malay, English, Mandarin or Tamil, no sign-up, no camera. Mamak nights, Manglish and when Malaysia is online.
- [Kenya](https://talklive.app/countries/kenya): Free voice and text chat with people in Kenya - in English, Kiswahili or Sheng, no sign-up, no camera. Greetings, topics, safety and when Kenya is online.
- [South Africa](https://talklive.app/countries/south-africa): Free voice and text chat with people in South Africa - howzit in any of twelve languages, no sign-up, no camera. Slang, rugby, the braai and when SA is online.

## Languages
The app UI and a localized homepage are available in: English plus [Español](https://talklive.app/es/), [Português](https://talklive.app/pt/), [Français](https://talklive.app/fr/), [Deutsch](https://talklive.app/de/), [Русский](https://talklive.app/ru/), [Türkçe](https://talklive.app/tr/), [العربية](https://talklive.app/ar/), [हिन्दी](https://talklive.app/hi/), [اردو](https://talklive.app/ur/), [Bahasa Indonesia](https://talklive.app/id/), [中文](https://talklive.app/zh/), [日本語](https://talklive.app/ja/), [한국어](https://talklive.app/ko/), [Italiano](https://talklive.app/it/), [فارسی](https://talklive.app/fa/), [বাংলা](https://talklive.app/bn/).

## Regional and language features
- [Why South Asia Talks After Midnight](https://talklive.app/regions/south-asia): One time zone stretched across India, three scripts that are slow to type, and a shared spoken language split by a border. Why conversation in South Asia happens late, and out loud.
- [Where the Weekend Moved: Talking Across the Middle East](https://talklive.app/regions/middle-east): Saudi Arabia moved its weekend in 2013, the UAE in 2022. Arabic is one written language and many spoken ones. Why the Middle East and North Africa talk on a different week, and late into the night.
- [Southeast Asia Runs an Hour Ahead of the Sun](https://talklive.app/regions/southeast-asia): Malaysia and Singapore moved their clocks in 1982 and never moved back. Indonesia spans three time zones. The Philippines once sent more text messages than almost anywhere. How Southeast Asia talks, and when.
- [Africa Reinvented the Phone Call](https://talklive.app/regions/africa): The missed call that means "call me back", money sent by text message, Swahili and Pidgin spoken by tens of millions, and the youngest population on Earth. How Africa talks, and why voice comes first.
- [Europe Runs on Four Clocks and Argues About All of Them](https://talklive.app/regions/europe): Spain keeps Berlin time for a reason dating to 1940. The EU voted to stop changing the clocks and never did. A data-led look at how sixteen European countries share one evening.
- [One Evening, Two Continents](https://talklive.app/regions/americas): New York and São Paulo are 7,700 km apart and an hour apart on the clock. How north and south America share an evening, why a Brazilian understands more Spanish than the reverse, and what "vos" tells you.
- [Seventeen Ways to Say Hello](https://talklive.app/languages/): A research feature on the 17 languages people use on TalkLive: scripts, word order, how many hours each takes an English speaker to learn, and the stubborn gap between understanding a language and speaking it.

## Blog
- [Why It Is Sometimes Easier to Tell a Stranger the Truth](https://talklive.app/blog/why-talking-to-strangers-feels-easier): People confess things to strangers on trains that they never tell their friends. A sociologist noticed this in 1908. Here is what is going on, and where it stops working.
- [The Rise and Fall of Omegle: Fourteen Years of Talking to Strangers](https://talklive.app/blog/what-happened-to-omegle): An 18-year-old built Omegle in his bedroom in 2009. It closed in November 2023 with a note about cost, misuse and a heart attack in his thirties. How it got there, and what it left behind.
- [We Are Bad at Predicting How Talking to Strangers Will Feel](https://talklive.app/blog/science-of-talking-to-strangers): Commuters, coffee queues and first conversations: a decade of experiments shows people consistently underestimate how much they will enjoy talking to strangers. Six studies, and their limits.
- [Loneliness Is Not the Same as Being Alone](https://talklive.app/blog/loneliness-what-actually-helps): You can be lonely in a full house and content on your own. What loneliness really is, why it makes people pull away, and the surprising finding about which kinds of help work best.
- [What Actually Happens in the Two Seconds After You Press "Start"](https://talklive.app/blog/how-random-matchmaking-works): A plain-English tour of a random voice match: the waiting queue, why filters make you wait, the handshake that connects two browsers, and the relay that carries the audio when a direct line is impossible.
- [Listening Is a Skill. Most of Us Were Never Taught It.](https://talklive.app/blog/how-to-be-a-good-listener): Why we interrupt, the "shift response" that quietly steals conversations, and what research says about the single habit that makes people like you more. Ten questions about listening.
- ["Why Does My Heart Race Every Time the Phone Rings?"](https://talklive.app/blog/phone-anxiety-how-to-get-comfortable-talking): A reader cannot make or answer phone calls without dread. Our reply on why calls are genuinely harder than texting, the habit that keeps the fear alive, and a step-by-step ladder out of it.
- [Why You Understand More Than You Can Say](https://talklive.app/blog/how-to-practise-a-language-by-speaking): Most learners can follow far more than they can say. A linguist called this out in 1985. Field notes on why speaking is its own skill, the fear that blocks it, and a four-week routine.
- [A Field Guide to the Scams That Start With "Hi"](https://talklive.app/blog/how-to-spot-a-bot-or-scam-in-random-chat): Romance-to-crypto schemes, image blackmail, the "send me the code" trick and the bots that never answer a question. Seven common specimens, how to recognise each, and the one rule that defeats nearly all of them.
- [30 Questions That Get Past Small Talk](https://talklive.app/blog/what-to-talk-about-with-a-stranger): In 1997 a psychologist made strangers feel close in 45 minutes with a list of questions that slowly got deeper. The idea behind it, why "what do you do?" stalls, and thirty questions in three tiers.
- [Why Boredom Hurts So Much, and What It Is Trying to Tell You](https://talklive.app/blog/why-am-i-so-bored): In one experiment, people chose to give themselves electric shocks rather than sit alone with their thoughts for fifteen minutes. What boredom really is, why scrolling rarely fixes it, and what does.
- [How to End a Conversation Without Being Rude](https://talklive.app/blog/how-to-end-a-conversation): Almost no conversation ends when both people want it to. What a Harvard study found about conversations that run too long or too short, how linguists describe a good goodbye, and exact words to use, in person, on a call or with a stranger online.
- [The Introvert's Guide to Talking to Strangers](https://talklive.app/blog/introvert-guide-to-talking-to-strangers): Introverts enjoy talking to strangers more than they predict, and pay for it later. What the research on acting extraverted actually shows, how to budget your social battery, and a gentle way to start.
- [Small Talk Around the World: What to Say, and What Not to Ask](https://talklive.app/blog/small-talk-around-the-world): Why "Have you eaten?" means hello in China, why Finns are fine with silence, and why Koreans ask your age. A passport of greetings, safe openers and questions to save for later in 12 countries.
- [Why One Phone Call Beats Fifty Texts](https://talklive.app/blog/why-a-call-beats-texting): People pick texting because they expect calls to be awkward. Experiments say they are wrong: a voice builds more connection, carries tone that text loses, and even changes stress hormones. What the research shows, and the myth it replaces.
- [New City, No One to Call: Loneliness After Moving Abroad](https://talklive.app/blog/lonely-after-moving-abroad): Around 280 million people live outside the country they were born in, and loneliness is one of the most common things they share. The real shape of culture shock, the two kinds of loneliness, and a practical plan for the first months.
